_comment: LoopStar GENERATIVE material pack. Genre DNA read at runtime by LoopStarMaterialEngine's on-device 'Make it new' generator. CONTENT, not code — zero-rebuild (RULE #1). Edit here, PR to mchatai-source; next cache refresh picks it up.
name: Dubstep
blurb: Half-time menace at 140 that breathes like 70 — cavernous sub, iron snare, and a whole lot of dark air.

flavors.label: Dungeon Deep
flavors.blurb: One minor chord held forever, meditation-slow, all the weight in the sub.

flavors.label: Riddim Slam
flavors.blurb: Root and b2, hit like a hammer, quantised to within an inch of its life.

flavors.label: Skanky Two-Step
flavors.blurb: Garage in its blood: i to bVI, short off-beat stabs, shuffled and human.

flavors.label: Purple Wonk
flavors.blurb: Bristol purple — actual chord changes, fat synth 9ths, everything slightly drunk.

flavors.label: Melodic Anthem
flavors.blurb: Big ringing i-bVI-bVII pads over the wobble — the festival drop with a tune.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: Dubstep is minor and nearly motionless: a single i drone under the sub does most of the work, with bVI, bVII and the phrygian bII as the only real moves, up to four bars a chord. No major keys, no V7, no maj7. The purple and melodic strains add m7 and m9 pads, but the root still rules the tune.
